session.question: In the context of OSC, what does the systematic review say about its environmental performance, its market penetration by 2018, and why is it considered timely to identify the factors that advanced and enhanced its environmental performance in developed and developing regions?
session.answer:
The systematic review reports that off-site construction (OSC) has clear environmental benefits, including reduced waste generation, lower carbon emissions, and improved environmental performance overall. Despite these advantages, by 2018 no major market had exceeded 20% OSC penetration. (jayawardana2023environmentalsustainabilityof chunk 1)

It is considered timely to identify the factors that advanced and enhanced OSC’s environmental performance because adoption remained relatively low even though the environmental benefits were already evidenced. The authors argue that examining these factors across developed and developing regions can reveal key learnings, strategies, critical success factors, and regional differences that may help increase OSC adoption and strengthen environmental sustainability. (jayawardana2023environmentalsustainabilityof chunk 1)

The review also frames this as an opportunity to address research gaps and improve future practice, including more comprehensive sustainability assessment, integration of smart and computerized technologies, study of prefabrication rates, and alignment with circular economy and Sustainable Development Goal (SDG) objectives. (jayawardana2023environmentalsustainabilityof chunk 1)

session.context:
pqac-822c5d90: The review states that off-site construction (OSC) has shown clear environmental benefits, including reduced waste generation and lower carbon emissions, and improved environmental performance more generally. Despite these advantages, by 2018 no major market had exceeded 20% OSC penetration. Because adoption remains relatively low even with proven benefits, the authors argue it is timely to identify the factors that have advanced and enhanced OSC’s environmental performance in both developed and developing regions. Doing so can reveal key learnings, strategies, critical success factors, and regional differences that may help increase OSC adoption and environmental sustainability.
From Janappriya Jayawardana, Asela K. Kulatunga, J. A. S. C. Jayasinghe, Malindu Sandanayake, and Guomin Zhang. Environmental sustainability of off-site construction in developed and developing regions: a systematic review. Journal of Architectural Engineering, 2023. URL: https://doi.org/10.1061/jaeied.aeeng-1420, doi:10.1061/jaeied.aeeng-1420.

pqac-bb55fbd6: The paper is a 2023 systematic review on the environmental sustainability of off-site construction (OSC), comparing developed and developing regions. It notes that OSC has recognized environmental benefits such as reduced waste generation and carbon emissions, but despite these advantages, no major market had exceeded 20% OSC penetration by 2018. The review uses bibliometric analysis and qualitative discussion to identify research trends, gaps, and critical success factors. It concludes that more work is needed on comprehensive sustainability assessments, smart/computerized technology integration, prefabrication-rate research, circular economy/SDG integration, and region-specific studies to improve environmental performance and adoption.
From Janappriya Jayawardana, Asela K. Kulatunga, J. A. S. C. Jayasinghe, Malindu Sandanayake, and Guomin Zhang. Environmental sustainability of off-site construction in developed and developing regions: a systematic review. Journal of Architectural Engineering, 2023. URL: https://doi.org/10.1061/jaeied.aeeng-1420, doi:10.1061/jaeied.aeeng-1420.

pqac-ba857be1: The excerpt is a 2021 systematic literature review on global value chains (GVCs) and the environmental sustainability of emerging market firms. It states that globalization of production creates both growth opportunities and environmental sustainability challenges. The review finds that GVCs play an important but dual and multilayered role in firms’ environmental sustainability, and that emerging market firms’ strategies, capabilities, and collaborative GVC relationships are important for implementing environmental practices. It also notes that the literature is fragmented and lacks theorization, and it proposes a research agenda.
From İsmail Gölgeci̇, Dilshod Makhmadshoev, and Mehmet Demirbağ. Global value chains and the environmental sustainability of emerging market firms: a systematic review of literature and research agenda. International Business Review, 2021. URL: https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ibusrev.2021.101857, doi:10.1016/j.ibusrev.2021.101857.

pqac-16bf53ae: The paper examines sustainability disclosure and environmental performance as predictors of market performance for non-financial companies listed on the Indonesian Stock Exchange from 2015 to 2019. Using panel regression on 32 companies participating in the KLHK PROPER award (160 observations), it finds that sustainability disclosure is not associated with market performance, but environmental performance is positively associated with market performance. The study is specific to Indonesia and focuses on market performance rather than market penetration. It suggests policy improvements by Indonesia’s financial and environmental authorities regarding sustainability-related company policies.
From Masayu Annisa Ihsani, Amrie Firmansyah, and Riska Septiana Estutik. Market response to companies sustainability disclosure and environmental performance in indonesia. Jurnal Dinamika Akuntansi dan Bisnis, 2021. URL: https://doi.org/10.24815/jdab.v8i2.21630, doi:10.24815/jdab.v8i2.21630.

pqac-c7e75560: The excerpt is a 2022 review on the renewable energy and sustainable development (RESD) nexus in developed and developing economies. It notes that most existing research focuses on developed countries and is often incompatible with developing nations. The paper reviews social and environmental boundaries across both types of economies and discusses how renewable energy can support sustainable growth under challenges like population growth, energy supply disruptions, and transportation shortages. It also frames the discussion around economic growth hypotheses, energy use, and renewable energy solutions. No specific mention of OSC, environmental performance, market penetration, or 2018 regional findings appears in the excerpt.
From Rabie Said, M. Ishaq Bhatti, and Ahmed Imran Hunjra. Toward understanding renewable energy and sustainable development in developing and developed economies: a review. Energies, 2022. URL: https://doi.org/10.3390/en15155349, doi:10.3390/en15155349.

contexts.context: The excerpt is a 2023 systematic review on sustainable supply chain management practices (SSCMPs) and environmental performance. It reviewed 140 journal articles from 2012–2022 using databases such as ABI/INFORM, ScienceDirect, SCOPUS, and DOAJ. The review found substantial evidence that SSCMPs positively affect environmental performance. It also noted that most studies focused on environmental sustainability, with less attention to operational and social performance. The authors recommend future research on social and operational performance as mediators, and suggest more industry-oriented studies using mixed methods and mediating/moderating variables.

contexts.context: The excerpt is a 2021 systematic literature review on global value chains (GVCs) and the environmental sustainability of emerging market firms. It states that globalization of production creates both growth opportunities and environmental sustainability challenges. The review finds that GVCs play an important but dual and multilayered role in firms’ environmental sustainability, and that emerging market firms’ strategies, capabilities, and collaborative GVC relationships are important for implementing environmental practices. It also notes that the literature is fragmented and lacks theorization, and it proposes a research agenda.

contexts.context: The paper is a 2023 systematic review on the environmental sustainability of off-site construction (OSC), comparing developed and developing regions. It notes that OSC has recognized environmental benefits such as reduced waste generation and carbon emissions, but despite these advantages, no major market had exceeded 20% OSC penetration by 2018. The review uses bibliometric analysis and qualitative discussion to identify research trends, gaps, and critical success factors. It concludes that more work is needed on comprehensive sustainability assessments, smart/computerized technology integration, prefabrication-rate research, circular economy/SDG integration, and region-specific studies to improve environmental performance and adoption.

session.formatted_answer:
Question: In the context of OSC, what does the systematic review say about its environmental performance, its market penetration by 2018, and why is it considered timely to identify the factors that advanced and enhanced its environmental performance in developed and developing regions?

The systematic review reports that off-site construction (OSC) has clear environmental benefits, including reduced waste generation, lower carbon emissions, and improved environmental performance overall. Despite these advantages, by 2018 no major market had exceeded 20% OSC penetration. (jayawardana2023environmentalsustainabilityof chunk 1)

It is considered timely to identify the factors that advanced and enhanced OSC’s environmental performance because adoption remained relatively low even though the environmental benefits were already evidenced. The authors argue that examining these factors across developed and developing regions can reveal key learnings, strategies, critical success factors, and regional differences that may help increase OSC adoption and strengthen environmental sustainability. (jayawardana2023environmentalsustainabilityof chunk 1)

The review also frames this as an opportunity to address research gaps and improve future practice, including more comprehensive sustainability assessment, integration of smart and computerized technologies, study of prefabrication rates, and alignment with circular economy and Sustainable Development Goal (SDG) objectives. (jayawardana2023environmentalsustainabilityof chunk 1)
